ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a large square, divided into four parts by a vertical line and a horizontal line: the upper-left part is the smaller square, the lower-right part is the larger square, and the upper-right and lower-left are rectangles. The gray quadrilateral is located near the intersection of the dividing lines; its upper and lower two vertices are on the vertical dividing line, and its left and right two vertices are on the horizontal dividing line; these vertices correspond to the midpoints of the sides of the two small squares mentioned in the problem. Reasoning: Let the side length of the upper-left small square be a, and the side length of the lower-right small square be b, then the side length of the large square is a + b. The two diagonals of the gray quadrilateral are horizontal and vertical respectively, and are perpendicular to each other. Since the vertices are the midpoints of the corresponding sides, each diagonal crosses half of the total side length of the large square, so the lengths of both diagonals are (a + b)/2. Area of the gray quadrilateral = 1/2 × (a + b)/2 × (a + b)/2 = (a + b)^2/8. The problem gives the gray area as 3, so (a + b)^2/8 = 3, obtaining the area of the large square (a + b)^2 = 24. Area of the non-shaded part = 24 - 3 = 21.

method.method_draft: From the image, read that one vertical and one horizontal segment divide the large square into a small square in the upper-left, a larger square in the lower-right, and two rectangles. Let the side lengths of the two smaller internal squares be a and b, so the big square has side a + b. From the text, use that the shaded quadrilateral’s vertices are the midpoints of the relevant sides of these two squares and its area is 3. The shaded quadrilateral has horizontal and vertical diagonals joining opposite midpoint vertices. Each diagonal spans half of the total big-square side, so both diagonals have length (a + b)/2. Since the diagonals are perpendicular, shaded area = 1/2 * ((a + b)/2) * ((a + b)/2) = (a + b)^2/8. Set this equal to 3, giving big square area (a + b)^2 = 24. Therefore the non-shaded area is 24 - 3 = 21.
